request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 83-year-old woman with a history of developmental disorders, presented to the emergency outpatient unit with a one-week history of dyspnea. She had heavily decreased breath sounds in the left lung. Chest radiograph and CT scan of the chest showed pleural effusions on the left lung. Two diagnostic thoracenteses were non-diagnostic, and a semirigid thoracoscopy was performed to visualize the pleura. Thoracoscopy revealed diffuse thickening of the parietal and visceral pleura, compatible with pleural dissemination with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma with malignant neoplasm. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged to the care of her family. 

Condition:
The patient had a stable condition upon discharge. 

Clinical Course:
The patient required semirigid thoracoscopy with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.

Follow-up:
The patient was referred for follow-up care with an oncologist. 

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow-up with an oncologist. 

Treatment:
The patient underwent semirigid thoracoscopy for biopsy samples, which was successful. The treatment plan includes referral to an oncologist for further management. 

Complications:
No complications were noted during the hospitalization.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The workup was for dyspnea and a left pleural effusion. Biopsy confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, with pleural dissemination seen at thoracoscopy. The condition established after investigation as chiefly responsible for the admission is therefore the lung adenocarcinoma.

Lung adenocarcinoma codes to C34 (malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung). The pleural involvement is a secondary neoplasm and would be coded separately as C78.2. The effusion is a malignant pleural effusion, which is integral to the pleural metastasis and is not sequenced as principal.

Since the primary site is established as lung and the pleural disease is secondary, C34 is the principal diagnosis.

CODE: C34
